title: Honor your friends (Berakhot 28b)
hook: Rabbi Eliezer's students ask for life's paths; he answers: be careful of your friends' honor
tomorrow: his students call him the lamp of Israel. so why is he crying?

segments.voice: Yesterday, Gamliel walked to Joshua's house and saw the soot: go to their house. Today the whole week comes back, with one more teacher's answer.
screen: `GO TO THEIR HOUSE.` → `THE WEEK COMES BACK.`

segments.voice: Graduation speakers get a few minutes to tell a room what matters most. Rabbi Eliezer gets a harder version. He's sick in bed, his students come to visit, and they ask him: teach us the paths of life. His first answer isn't about prayer, and it isn't about study. It's this: be careful with your friends' honor.
screen: `WHAT MATTERS MOST?` → `A TEACHER, SICK IN BED.` → `FIRST: YOUR FRIENDS' HONOR.`

segments.voice: He goes on. Keep your children from higayon, a word readers explain in different ways. Seat them at the knees of the sages. And when you pray, know before whom you stand. Four paths, and the friend comes first. Now look back at this week, because it kept circling the same place. Mar's own prayer asked God to guard his tongue. Rava called himself dust while alive. The sages of Yavneh said much or little, the heart, and wouldn't look down on the man in the field. Rav's world to come had no jealousy and no competition. Then Gamliel shamed one student, the doors opened, and he walked to Joshua's house to ask forgiveness. Rabbi Eliezer's first path is where all of it lands. A friend's honor is easy to break and worth guarding, and it's yours to guard. Here's the line to tell a friend tonight. Asked for the way to the world to come, a sage didn't start with heaven. He started with the people sitting next to you.
screen: `FOUR PATHS OF LIFE.` · `THE FRIEND COMES FIRST.` · `THE WEEK, CIRCLING ONE PLACE.` · `START WITH WHO'S NEXT TO YOU.` · then, large: `HONOR YOUR FRIENDS.`

segments.voice: Count on your fingers the friends who've been good to you lately, one finger each. For each one, name a single thing about them worth honoring. If one name stings because you owe them something, hold that finger a little longer.
screen: `ONE FINGER, ONE FRIEND.` · `ONE THING WORTH HONORING.` · `HOLD THE ONE THAT STINGS.`

segments.voice: Honor your friends. Rabbi Eliezer's first path of life, said from a sickbed: be careful with your friends' honor.
Carry this: honor your friends, a sage's first path to the world to come. Eighteen of fifty, and a week of Berakhot behind you.

screen: `DAY 1505 COUNTS.` → `BERAKHOT · 18 OF 50.` → `TOMORROW: THEY CALL HIM THE LAMP OF ISRAEL. WHY IS HE CRYING?`

howItsDone: Jewish teaching counts guarding another person's dignity as a serious duty, and students of the Talmud often learn Rabbi Eliezer's four paths of life together as a short list to live by.

fork.reveal: be careful with your friends' honor: in Berakhot 28b, it's the first path of life, and it's yours to guard.

original.note: Hebrew: be careful with the honor of your friends. Rabbi Eliezer's first path of life.

what a scholar hears: Berakhot 28b gives four paths: friends' honor, children kept from higayon, the knees of the sages, and know before whom you stand; readers differ on higayon.

chat.says: went to owen's. we're ok now. but i embarrassed him in front of the cast. is private enough?
options: Guard his honor where you hurt it: give him real credit in front of the cast.
Private was enough; praising him in public now would just make it weird.
Give him a bigger part; honoring friends means friends get the best roles.
chat.meaning: Rabbi Eliezer's first path is to be careful with your friends' honor. The wrong was public, so the honor can be restored in public too.
